title: "Interval overlap across 435 pairs"

description: "Comparison of marginal interval overlap and direction probabilities in a thirty-unit simulation."
---

Across all 435 pairs in the thirty-unit [shrunk league](shrinkage.qmd), marginal credible intervals frequently overlap even when the posterior favors one direction with probability above .90.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Overlap, highest probability.** 399 of 435 pairs overlap at 90%, and 88 favor one direction above .90 — led by U13 above U05 at .988 (overlap .00549).
- **U06 and U20.** Intervals lie .00219 apart with Pr(U06 > U20) = .988, matching the top overlapping pair.
- **U04 and U18.** Overlap .107 yet Pr(U04 > U18) = .904: U18 ends at −.105, below U04's mean (−.0143).
- **95% intervals.** 413 pairs overlap, 102 above .90, led by U03 above U15 at .997.
- **Prior SD .05.** Stronger shrinkage yields 427 overlapping pairs, 58 above .90.

<details>
<summary>Probability bounds and source note</summary>

For two independent normal posteriors, whatever their SDs, the more likely direction has probability above .950 when their 90% intervals do not overlap, and at most .990 when they overlap (.975 and .997 for 95% intervals). Kline, Rose and Walters (2024, section IV.C) draw a credible interval beside each name, while grading names from pairwise posterior probabilities.

</details>
